segments.title: The Duisburg or Beta Convoy carried supplies for Axis armies in North Africa
segments.body: The Duisburg Convoy, also called the Beta Convoy, was one of the regular Axis supply sailings across the Mediterranean. It carried supplies for German and Italian forces in North Africa. The Italian troops depended on these shipments just as the German forces did. The Italian formations are tentatively identified as the Fifth and Tenth Armies.

evidence.note: The video identifies the Duisburg Convoy as the Beta Convoy, describes regular German and Italian supply sailings, and tentatively names the Italian Fifth and Tenth Armies.

segments.summary: The Duisburg Convoy, also called the Beta Convoy, was one of the regular Mediterranean sailings intended to supply German and Italian forces in North Africa.

segments.title: Cracked codes and Malta reconnaissance expose the convoy
segments.body: British intelligence learned of the sailing from cracked Enigma traffic and Italian codes, giving two confirmations. An RAF reconnaissance aircraft was then sent to find the convoy in plain sight. The sighting offered the Axis a plausible explanation for the interception and helped conceal the compromised communications. Because reconnaissance aircraft from Malta seemed repeatedly to find convoys, Axis forces overestimated how many were operating there. That error also inflated their estimate of Malta's garrison.

evidence.note: Codebreaking directed RAF reconnaissance toward Axis convoys, and the repeated sightings led the Axis to overestimate Malta's reconnaissance capacity.

segments.summary: Cracked Enigma and Italian codes revealed the sailing, while an RAF reconnaissance aircraft gave the British a visible way to locate it without exposing the intelligence source.

segments.title: Aurora, Penelope, and Upholder strike the convoy
segments.body: The Arethusa-class light cruisers Aurora and Penelope sailed with two destroyers to intercept the convoy. The surface force wiped out the convoy in a single action. About 40,000 tons of shipping were sunk across several vessels. Upholder, a U-class submarine based at Malta, also took part.

evidence.note: Aurora, Penelope, and two destroyers sank about 40,000 tons of shipping, with the Malta-based submarine Upholder also joining the attack.

segments.summary: Aurora, Penelope, and two destroyers wiped out the convoy, sinking about 40,000 tons of shipping; the Malta-based submarine Upholder also joined the attack.
